comparison.objective: Both install spring-retained hardware into square rack openings, but candidate installs an entire rail at front and rear posts whereas the record installs one cage fastener in a coupon.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require compressing/depressing a spring feature and aligning retaining elements through rack holes. Candidate additionally tests long-rail support, paired-prong insertion at two separated posts, telescoping, leveling, regrasping, and screw fastening.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires correct handedness, four prongs, full spring extension, matched rack units, bottom-hole screws, and self-support; record requires recorded leg compression, both hooks through one opening, fixture immobility, gripper release, and stability.
comparison.reason: This is the closest spring-rack neighbor, but its central test is a single cage-fastener leg-compression insertion; the candidate's defining tested ability is staged load-bearing rail registration across two posts. Candidate still lacks numeric prong travel, force, pose, and damage thresholds, so distinction depends on preserving the full multi-post sequence.
